request: What public functions or types does clients/store/src/index.ts re-export from derivation.ts and descriptor.ts, and are there any internal-only symbols excluded from the public API?

final_json.interpretation: Which public functions/types index.ts re-exports from derivation.ts and descriptor.ts, and which symbols are excluded as internal-only

snippets.why: The barrel: re-exports parseStorageDescriptor + 5 types from descriptor.js and postgresDatabaseName/sqliteStorePath from derivation.js
Exported public types: StorageDescriptor, Isolation, StorageBackend, SqliteStorageBackend, PostgresStorageBackend (all re-exported)
Exported parseStorageDescriptor (re-exported) — the public parse entry point
Internal-only symbols NOT re-exported: JsonRecord type, and helpers parseIsolation/parseBackend/expectRecord/expectString/descriptorError (all non-exported)
Exported postgresDatabaseName and sqliteStorePath — the two functions re-exported by index.ts
Internal-only module constants (FNV_OFFSET_BASIS_64, FNV_PRIME_64, MASK_64, textEncoder) not exported
Internal-only helpers not exported: postgresSlug, isAsciiAlphanumeric, fnv1a64Hex

request: In text-animations-word-highlight.tsx, what happens to the highlight index/state calculation when the current frame exceeds the total duration derived from word count times per-word duration — does the logic clamp, wrap, or throw?

final_json.interpretation: How the highlight index/state is computed when the current frame exceeds a word-count × per-word total duration, and whether it clamps/wraps/throws.

snippets.why: Highlight progress comes from a Remotion spring; the resulting scaleX is explicitly clamped with Math.max(0, Math.min(1, highlightProgress)) — it clamps, never wraps or throws.
highlightIndex here is FULL_TEXT.indexOf(HIGHLIGHT_WORD) — a character position, not a frame- or word-count-derived index; slice bounds are guarded by hasHighlight (>= 0).

omissions.what: No word-count × per-word-duration total-duration calculation exists in this file
omissions.detail: The animation is single-word and spring-driven with a fixed delay/durationInFrames; there is no total = wordCount * perWordDuration term and no frame-vs-total comparison to clamp/wrap/throw on, so the request's premise does not hold for this file.
